edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), Ad Scapulam, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Nos quidem neque expavescimus, neque pertimescimus ea, quae ab ignorantibus patimur: cum ad hanc sectam, utique suscepta conditione ejus, pacti venerimus, ut etiam animas nostras auctorati in has pugnas accedamus, ea quae Deus repromittit consequi optantes, et ea quae diversae vitae comminatur pati timentes. Denique cum omni saevitia vestra concertamus, etiam ultro erumpentes, magisque damnati quam absoluti gaudemus. Itaque hunc libellum non nobis timentes misimus, sed vobis et omnibus inimicis nostris, nedum amicis: ita enim disciplina jubemur diligere inimicos quoque, et orare pro eis qui nos persequuntur: ut haec sit perfecta et propria bonitas nostra, non communis. Amicos enim diligere omnium est, inimicos autem solorum christianorum. Qui ergo dolemus de ignorantia vestra, et miseremur erroris humani, et futura prospicimus, et signa eorum quotidie intentari videmus, necesse est vel hoc modo erumpere ad proponenda vobis ea, quae palam non vultis audire.
pass_a_gloss: We indeed neither are frightened nor do we fear those things which we suffer from ignorant people: since to this sect, certainly with its condition accepted, we have come, so that we also, having pledged our souls, approach these battles, wishing to attain those things which God promises, and fearing to suffer those things which a different life threatens. Finally, since we contend with all your savagery, and even bursting forth voluntarily, we rejoice more when condemned than when acquitted. And so we have sent this little book not because we fear for ourselves, but for you and all our enemies, not to mention friends: for we are commanded by our discipline to love even enemies and to pray for those who persecute us: so that this may be our perfect and proper goodness, not common. For loving friends is common to all, but loving enemies is unique to Christians. Therefore, since we grieve over your ignorance, and we pity human error, and we look to the future, and we see the signs of these things being prepared every day, it is necessary for us to burst forth in this way to propose to you those things which you do not want to hear openly.

choices.why: indicates friends are not the primary target

pass_b_english: We are not frightened, nor do we fear what we suffer at the hands of ignorant people. We embraced this sect precisely on its terms, pledging our souls so we could enter these battles—hoping to gain what God promises and dreading what a different life threatens. We meet your every cruelty head-on, even volunteering for the fight, and we rejoice more when condemned than when acquitted. That is why we sent this pamphlet: not because we fear for ourselves, but for you and all our enemies—not to mention our friends. Our discipline commands us to love even enemies and to pray for those who persecute us, so that our goodness may be perfect and distinctive, not ordinary. Everyone loves their friends; only Christians love their enemies. Since we grieve over your ignorance, pity human error, watch the future, and see the signs of these things being prepared daily, we must break out in this way to lay before you what you refuse to hear openly.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English version that maintains the agency and distinctions of the original (e.g., 'not to mention friends' for 'nedum amicis' and the distinction between 'common' and 'proper/distinctive' goodness).
